turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come through, you can sit. The corridor's a bit chaotic this morning. What brings you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Shame, doctor, it's the burning when I wee. Again. Properly sore. We got stuck at that robot by the mall, the lights were out, I nearly told her to turn around.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): We made it, though. I'm her carer, I come in most weekdays. She's been fidgety in the car.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Glad you didn't turn around. The burning, is it every time you pass urine, or just now and then?

[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Every time. And I'm going often, just little bits, and I'm up at night, three times last night. The dog next door, a ridgeback, was barking at nothing, so between the dog and the toilet I got no sleep. He's a lovely animal, just loud.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did this round start? Can you put a day on it?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, I can't. Since the long weekend, or maybe before that. I thought it was after I did the big wash, but I honestly don't know which day.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I can't date it either. She mentioned it when I came to do the shopping, around that long weekend, but I never wrote the day down.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): So we're both guessing on the start. Any blood in the urine at all?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No blood. Just that hot sting. Oh, and I feel washed out, a bit tired, nothing dramatic.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever? Pain over the back, where the kidneys sit? Any nausea sitting with you now?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. Back's fine. I'm not nauseous. My stomach only plays up if I take the wrong tablet, but that's an old story.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll come to tablets. Any vaginal discharge, or itching down there?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that, hey. No itch, no discharge. It's the urine, full stop.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fair enough. Has the burning happened before this year?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Third time this year. Ja. I'm sixty-two, I should be past this nonsense. My cousin says it's from sitting on cold benches, which is rubbish, but she means well.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Wait, hang on. Maybe the fourth. I forgot the one after the Christmas visitors left. So maybe four, not three. Sorry.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Possibly four episodes this year, then. What have you actually taken for this one?

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Um. This is the embarrassing bit. I took my sister's leftover antibiotic. I know, I know. She's in Durban, she had the same burning when she visited, and the box stayed in my cupboard.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which antibiotic, do you remember the name?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Ciprofloxacin, I think. Those white tablets. I think they were 500 milligrams, and I took them morning and night.
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The box said ciprofloxacin 500. Morning and night for three days, then the strip was empty. I saw her finish them.

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, I stopped when they ran out. It eased a tiny bit, then the burn came straight back. So that was a waste. Her bakkie's still at the panel beater, not that you need that.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hmm. Alright, my first thought is the usual one. I'll start nitrofurantoin today and we'll dip the urine here in the room. That often sorts a simple bladder infection.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Nitrofurantoin? Ag, no. I stopped that in March. Made me feel really sick, so I only managed two days and I left the rest.
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She was green around the gills on it. We didn't try it again.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stopped in March for nausea, only two days. Was there any other script you were given and didn't use?

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Fosfomycin. The little sachet. I never took it. It's still sitting in the drawer, unopened. I didn't fancy it. And there's cranberry juice in the fridge I bought and forgot, so that doesn't count either.
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The sachet is definitely unopened. She has been taking Panado, two of the 500 milligram tablets, when the stinging gets bad.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, not on a schedule. Once or twice a day the last few days, only if I need it. Rooibos doesn't count, I just like it.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines? Rashes, swelling, that sort of thing?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing. I can take most stuff. The nitrofurantoin was a sick tummy, not an allergy, I'm sure of that.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. No known drug allergies. Let me think this out loud, because I'm going to change what I just said. You've already had three days of ciprofloxacin and you're still burning, and nitrofurantoin made you nauseous. If I start that again I'll probably just make you ill, and another blind antibiotic on top of cipro is a bad idea.

[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): So scratch the nitrofurantoin and scratch the dip. No antibiotic from me today. I'll send a proper urine sample to the lab for microscopy and culture, and we wait to see what grows.

[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No tablets? I have to just sit with it? We're supposed to go to my cousin's braai on Saturday, and I can't be queuing for the loo the whole afternoon. Also load shedding keeps tripping the fridge, the meat might not even survive, but that's her problem.

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): I know the braai matters. The trouble is a wrong tablet now can spoil the culture and still leave you sore. Drink plenty of water through the day. And please don't take anyone else's antibiotics again, even if the box is sitting there.
[SEG0037] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll park the water bottle next to her chair. She forgets when she gets talking.

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I do talk, ja. Doctor, um. I need to unsay something. I said there was no itching. There is a bit. Down there. And a little whitish discharge. I was embarrassed, that's why I said no.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm glad you came back to it. How long has the itch been there, and the discharge?

[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): The itch, a few days I think. Same muddy timing as the burning, I can't separate them. Discharge is whitish, not a lot. No bad smell that I've noticed. No sores. I'm not bleeding.
[SEG0041] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She told me not to mention it. She was shifting around in the car the whole way, though.

[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Itch and a small whitish discharge, no smell you've noticed, no sores, no bleeding. That can travel with a urine infection, or it can be thrush, or something else vaginal. I'm not ready to call it.

[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): I had thrush years ago, after some antibiotic, ages back. This feels more like the burn is from the wee. I hope it's not both. And the garden is a mess, she's been watering because I haven't had the energy, the weeds are up to my knees.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): One problem at a time. I'm going to feel your tummy now. Say if I hit a sore spot.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Abdomen's soft. Mild tenderness low down over the bladder. No tenderness in either loin.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vitals from a moment ago, while you were settling. Temperature 36.7, pulse 76, blood pressure 132 over 78. That's not a fever.

[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. My late husband was the one with the high blood pressure, always fussing with the machine. I don't have that. I just get this bladder thing. He used to braai better than my cousin, mind you.

[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Working impression, and I mean working, not final. This is probably a lower urine infection, from the burning, the frequency, and that bladder tenderness. With the discharge I also can't rule out a vaginal infection, thrush included. We'll let the test talk.
[SEG0049] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Do you still only want the urine, now that she's admitted the discharge? I thought swabs were a thing.

[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): I did consider adding a vaginal swab just now. I'm not adding it today. Urine microscopy, culture and sensitivity is the test I'm ordering. If the culture comes back negative and the discharge is still bothering you, then we can swab.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): So I just wee in a cup? Midway through, someone once told me. I always mess that up.
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ja, midstream, in the cup they'll give you at the desk on the way out. It's ordered now, the form goes with you. Not a dip in the room, the lab one.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): And the Panado, do I carry on with those?
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): Carry on. Two of the 500 milligram tablets when you need them, and don't go past four times in a day. No more ciprofloxacin unless a result makes me script it.
[SEG0055] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And if she gets worse before you have the result? She won't always tell me.

[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back in three days and we'll go through the result. That's the plan, I'll book it. If you spike a fever, start vomiting, or the pain shifts into your back before then, come straight in, don't wait for the three days.

[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Three days. I'll try not to google myself into a state. Last time I was convinced it was something hectic. We can skip Dis-Chem. Just the water. Thank you, doctor, sorry for the long story.

spec.situation: Woman with burning urine again; says 'third time this year' then corrects to 'maybe the fourth'; took leftover antibiotic from a sister; embarrassed; vaginal symptoms denied, then partly admitted. Urine test ordered.
features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

bad.reason: Burning, sore, every time is stated; certainty is not uncertain.
bad.text: burning when passing urine (category=genitourinary, status=present, severity=properly sore, frequency=every time she passes urine, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=uncertain)

omissions.text: Nitrofurantoin caused significant nausea/'really sick' and was stopped in March after only 2 days; patient stated this was a side effect and not an allergy.
Fosfomycin sachet had previously been prescribed but was never taken and remains unopened in the drawer.
Initial plan to start nitrofurantoin and do an in-room urine dip was explicitly changed: nitrofurantoin was cancelled, the urine dip was cancelled, and no antibiotic was prescribed today.

Negative findings initially given for vaginal symptoms were revised by the patient: she first denied itching and discharge, then corrected herself to say there is some itching and a little whitish discharge because she had been embarrassed.
Discharge details missing: it was described as 'not a lot' and with no bad smell noticed.
Negative finding missing: no urinary/vaginal sores.
Past history relevant to differential: previous thrush years ago after taking an antibiotic.
